messages.subject: Proportional Bar Charts
parts:
Hi,

First of all, thanks for ggplot2, it's really great!

Now I have a question. I want to construct a bar chart that shows
proportions instead of counts. I'm looking at the ggplot2 book, at
Figure 2.15 on page 21, which shows what I want. I can re-create that
figure fine.

However I want to do the same thing with a factor variable, e.g. Sex:

This works fine:
qplot(Sex, ..count.., data=dat.complete, geom="bar")

But this doesn't:
qplot(Sex, ..density.., data=dat.complete, geom="bar")

Well, something gets plotted, but there are just two equal height
bars, rather than the proportions of males and females. I've read the
examples, web site and man pages as much as I can stand, and I can't
see what I'm missing.

Any clues?

Thanks in advance

John

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Proportional Bar Charts
parts:
Hi John,

The reason is simple, but fairly subtle - it's because of the default
grouping behaviour. By default ggplot splits up the data according to
the combination of levels of all the categorical variables on the plot
- so in your case you get a dataset for each bar, and so the density
is just n / n = 1. The way to get around this is to override the
default grouping so that there is a single group for the whole
dataset:

qplot(cut, data = diamonds, geom = "bar")
qplot(cut, ..density.., data = diamonds, geom = "bar")
qplot(cut, ..density.., data = diamonds, geom = "bar", group = 1)

I realise this isn't very obvious, but I don't think I can change the
default behaviour with out breaking things in other places.

Regards,

Hadley
